changes.before: If the text passed to write_note changes to rest, what is read after it returns?
changes.after: A connection is an open path for reading or writing data. Finish using the writer before reading the file again.

before: A connection represents an input or output stream. file(path, open = "wt") opens a text-writing connection; close releases it. Inside a function, on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE) registers cleanup even if the body errors.

file.path joins path components using platform conventions, not an authorization policy. writeLines writes text lines to the connection; readLines reads them after the writer is closed. The example owns a disposable relative path and never accepts a user-supplied traversal path.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
write_note <- function(path, text) {
  con <- file(path, open = "wt")
  on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  writeLines(text, con)
}
path <- file.path(".", "note.txt")
write_note(path, "read")
cat(readLines(path), "\n", sep = "")

```
Expected output or behavior: read. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

before.question: If the text passed to write_note changes to rest, what is read after it returns?
choices: rest, after the writer connection has been closed.
Nothing because a closed connection deletes its file.
before.explanation: Cleanup closes the stream but does not roll back or delete the completed file; the new line remains available to read.

after.question: After the writer closes, which word does readLines get?
after.explanation: The file now contains the newly written word.
